84.4% of all untested tools sit in three repositories, each shipping a large tool catalogue. Pooling across repositories of very different sizes describes the ecosystem's tool population rather than a typical project. Capped means the per-repository read limit bound, so that repository's coverage is an upper bound.

Read the intervals, not the ordering. Several categories hold fewer than 20 tools and their intervals overlap heavily. The claim is only that the extremes separate: version-control and shell tools are less covered than database and filesystem tools.

What screened out, and why it matters

A repository enters the analysed set only if the detectors find at least one write-capable tool definition. Screening is mechanical: 32 of 45 candidates were excluded by the code, not by hand.

This is the study's dominant limitation. Screening out is not a claim that a project performs no writes — it means the project exposes no framework-idiomatic tool definition whose body performs a detectable write. Agents with bespoke architectures write to disk and shell out constantly but expose no @tool or BaseTool surface. The denominator of 13 reflects detector coverage as much as the ecosystem.

Screened out: Aider-AI/aider, All-Hands-AI/OpenHands, AntonOsika/gpt-engineer, assafelovic/gpt-researcher, browser-use/browser-use, deepset-ai/haystack, entropy-research/Devon, huggingface/smolagents, kyegomez/swarms, langchain-ai/langchain, langchain-ai/langgraph, langroid/langroid, lavague-ai/LaVague, letta-ai/letta, mem0ai/mem0, microsoft/JARVIS, microsoft/TaskWeaver, microsoft/UFO, modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk, openai/swarm, OpenBMB/AgentVerse, OpenBMB/ChatDev, OpenInterpreter/open-interpreter, pydantic/pydantic-ai, Qodo-Ai/pr-agent, Skyvern-AI/skyvern, stanfordnlp/dspy, superagent-ai/superagent, SWE-agent/SWE-agent, sweepai/sweep, THUDM/AgentBench, yoheinakajima/babyagi

Reproduce it

git clone https://github.com/RithikSatarla/agentcage.git
cd agentcage && pip install -e ".[dev]"

python -m part_a.run          # the study, 45 repos at HEAD
python -m part_a.analyze      # intervals, categories, figures
pytest tests/                 # full suite, no network

The study costs 45 GitHub API calls, inside the unauthenticated hourly limit. Responses cache under .cache/, so a second run is nearly instant. It re-runs weekly in CI, and every push re-runs the pipeline against the live API.

Files are read at HEAD, so re-running later measures later code. This page was generated from the run of 2026-08-04.
